title: The Basket Heard the Figure Twice

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: A reading is not a payment and the end of a month is not a door. The basket hears the figure twice and carries home the weight of neither; the row stands where it stood.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Clay Yard, told at the going out of Grain

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and thirty-seven to two hundred and thirty-nine days, six months and fifty-seven days to six months and fifty-nine days, carried everywhere and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing --- the file turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing; a month's three readings held apart from the arithmetic paid and from the cost of the dressed grain; the ownerless question opened as a surgeon opens a wound and found to have no witness at the bottom; the carrying arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost; the body read at two paces, exact and worth nothing without a hand to carry it --- without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line; the old life stays offstage and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room or back-room interior, no hearing beyond six, no seventh of the full note, no tenth stopping before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, no fifth telling of the burned slate, no third telling of the counting room shut in the war, no fourth shaping of the pot saying, no fifth witness to the question, no eighth green or eighth shape, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no opening of the widow's mark, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read, no figure given for the dressed grain or the hand that did not come back, no name spoken over the green or the shape, no sale or betrayal paid and no ending

scenes.title: The Fifty-Seventh Day
scenes.synopsis: First of six entries, first dated heading and the chapter's only drop cap: Day 237, Grain 28, Eighthday, small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf and the Clay Yard. No recap: the hand lay down against the fold after the forty-eighth answer and that two-rhythm coordination is set down like a tool, never recalled as a sign, growth, reaching, gift or power. Count exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody at 236 going into **237**, six months and fifty-seven days, told by nobody (T071/T072); first smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that, with the sour Ash breath of the unswept corner the house calls the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. Three counts in three places --- the carried fire's four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should be under the floor (payer unnamed two hundred and thirty-seven days, T088), the river's note of water over water through the finger's-width door, the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot --- none rising into another, for agreeing them would want a payer and none stands to any (T061/T082). One stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform. The file is turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers, three shapings of the pot saying, the fourth burned-slate telling and the two shut-room tellings on their own places, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid with Grain's second arithmetic and the true subtraction in Berr's locked box answering nothing for the man carried out on Day 188, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, the Seed 16 breath unspent, three held changes plus the loft scrape, the carried man's pale line and the held inch, the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth, the dressed grain covered and unfigured and the returning-line place gone around with a look and no number. Sella goes to the fire before the basket, gives her instruction to wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never to the basket, says *the house* and *The house will keep it*, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, moves her lips along the two-gapped row without a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and leaves the widow's mark untouched --- no opening in **fifty-seven** days, because a morning, a shelf, a yard and a basket are not openings (T058/T079, T100). The dressed grain is turned under its wool for damp; a cost-question at the door goes to the pot and the weather and a fist's number come down the clay road goes back into its sleeve, arriving nowhere (T077). The hand is asked the first way of the chapter and answers the **forty-ninth** time --- down at once under conditions that have sometimes answered --- filed on the sixth place with no payer named, not a hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule (T061/T082). Emotional turn: the exactness of the small hours meets the ordinary work of the morning and the count goes forward though nobody speaks it. Last image: the hand comes down at once against the fold while Sella carries the unanswered cost-question away level toward the pot.

scenes.title: Six Where the House Can Check
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 237, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the salt coat and hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat settles under the low angle, behind the pot, into the fold where one stiff brown-edged barley crust lies two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform (T061/T082). Garl is kept in objects and not in a story: salt-stiff coat with the crease at the left shoulder, hollow seat with its twenty-year lean, the clean dark line and the finer grey called the thaw unswept, a proverb gone years ago to a pot with no crack, the tile debt circling without a name, his name unspoken two hundred and thirty-seven days; no collector came up or went down the clay road (T009/T013/T092). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed and tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, setting the small knife at the very edge of its sill: six in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it. The ear-sentence comes to his teeth and goes all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name --- a remembered stopping and not a new one --- nine stoppings stand with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath is drawn and not spent, the loan stays uncalled and no collector came on Grain 28; chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, pale clip-ring at the left wrist, warm stone cold and unreconciled in its unmarked loft pot in the Debt Loft, which reaches him as a sound with a direction and nothing more (T036/T076, T006). At the wheel-shed edge Jorra comes through with the day's meal-fine grey slate dust ground past the bent finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened, and not bone-coloured slip; dusty and clean forearms stay on one tray, the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack are entered by nobody, he speaks to the wheel and tells a pot *You'll do*, knows its full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, keeps the burned-slate word at four and the shut-room tellings at two, names neither the men who came low before first grey nor the room, and grows quieter as a low voice goes around the boards; when Sella's sentence goes low his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of it, holds until the end arrives at the pot, moves a hair's breadth and is left standing --- a remembered repetition and not a change made again (T035/T031/T062, T061/T082). At the going of the light Sella carries him home at the half-pace, woodsmoke before her in long low bars and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number; seven things standing in a row are still seven and not an account until a payer stands under them, and none does (T009/T013/T092, T098 advanced and not paid). She sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen and goes to her own bed before the small hours. In the small hours fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one. The hand is asked the second way and answers the **fiftieth** time --- held for the small intake only and down before the letting-go --- filed on the sixth place with no payer named, exact, complete and worth nothing (T061/T082). Emotional turn: the household's kept objects and the boy's kept file are the same discipline performed without either person knowing the other keeps it. Last image: the hand comes down before the letting-go while the fire behind the wall misses its fifth.

scenes.title: The Cover Goes Back Again
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 238, Grain 29, Ninthday, small hours under the Vail roof, then the ordinary morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the drying racks and the Clay Yard. New day, new date, no recap: **238** exact, six months and fifty-eight days, nobody told (T071/T072); fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and thirty-eight days (T088); first smell hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath of the corner called the thaw; first sound the kiln in fours with its gap, no bell, no market and no Cross, for Grain 30 stands one morning ahead. The dressed grain is turned under its wool for damp, looked at, spread thin to finish and gathered back by the handful, the fold set flat; it changes state and gains no figure, counted in glances and handfuls and by the carrying arm's weight that knows weight and not cost, entered on no slate and laid across none of the absences (T077). A neighbour at the threshold asks what the storing will take now the grain is under wool and Sella sends the question to the pot and the weather; a man come down the clay road brings a number up out of a fist toward the yard well, looks at it and puts it back into his sleeve, so the figure arrives nowhere; the figure read over the covered grain on Grain's second Account-day is still not the figure paid, and the true subtraction stays locked in Berr's box answering nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 (T015/T041/T047 held). A wrong wind comes up off High Kiln: the sweet edge of lead glaze rides over the boards, touches the fold and goes out on the wind that brought it, a direction arrived nowhere and not a second edge paid, the seventh green still a colour and the seventh shape still a shape with no eighth of either, no second look joined, no name spoken over either, no loaf, slate or sale, neither woman nor child called Fenna nor Ulda in the narration and no romance paid (T064, T050/T051 and T033/T034 held). One of the three shapings of the pot saying --- a pot gone quiet on every row come the thaw --- is let to stand again as a saying, for three likenesses must not stand up and call themselves a rule; the burned-slate word stays at four and the shut-room tellings at two (T061/T082, T035/T031/T065/T095). Sella moves her lips along the two-gapped row with no figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, and leaves the widow's mark where it hangs --- no opening in **fifty-eight** days, because a shelf, a strip, a rack, a yard and a basket are not openings (T058/T079, T100). The hand is asked the third way and answers the **fifty-first** time --- down before the counted breath had finished --- filed on the sixth place with no payer named (T061/T082). Emotional turn: a month that has kept its grain under wool for nine days prepares to be read over by a figure that does not know what it cost, and the boy cannot enter either figure. Last image: the cover goes back flat over the dressed grain while the sweet edge of glaze goes out on the wind that brought it.

scenes.title: The Fourth Asking
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 238, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the boards fronting the shelf, the hearth, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. THE CHAPTER'S SECOND ADVANCEMENT, unpaid and closely bounded --- **T101 gains a fourth asking and only one**: a voice with no owner, no room, no hand at the kiln and no cause comes over the boards again, low into the boards and not into the basket, asking which row the pot went quiet on. The weather answers first and the price of barley answers after it, and the voice goes off up the terrace toward High Kiln while the row stands where it stood --- a direction arrived nowhere, with nobody leaning in to take the answer down and no hand standing to it. The boy takes it apart as a surgeon takes apart a wound --- what it asks, where it stands, what it would want before any man could answer it, and who would have to stand under the answer to pay --- and finds no witness at the bottom, setting the fourth telling on the seventh place beside the first three with a finger between each pair, and a finger between them and the three shapings of the pot saying, the fourth burned-slate telling, the two shut-room tellings, the six hearings of the full note and the count. **Four askings are still not one witness; a witness stands somewhere and can be asked, and none does and none could.** It is NOT a fourth shaping of the pot saying, NOT a hearing, NOT a seventh of the full note, NOT a fifth telling of the slate, NOT a cause, NOT a name and NOT a fifth witness --- a seed for the far-off day a witness stands somewhere and can be asked (T101 advanced, unpaid). No fifth asking is to come in this chapter; the row is not named and no payer stands to the answer. The afternoon thins; heat settles under the low angle into the fold where one stiff brown-edged barley crust lies two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform (T061/T082). Garl stays in objects, his name unspoken two hundred and thirty-eight days and no collector on the clay road (T009/T013/T092). Sella gives the fire its instruction before the basket, tells it the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it* where another woman would say *I*, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and leaves the mark untouched with no opening in fifty-eight days (T058/T079). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, sets the knife at the very edge with six where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there as a remembered stopping with nine hold and no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, draws the Seed 16 breath and does not spend it, and sweeps the collector's road without once turning along it (T036/T076). Jorra's dust comes out of the shed, his full note known three turns ahead and withheld, his finger in the damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence as a remembered repetition, *he's not Vail* sealed and the promise of the boy's name neither given nor withdrawn (T035/T031/T062). The hand is asked the fourth way and answers the **fifty-second** time --- held through a whole counted breath at Sella's fire in the room that does not touch his and down with the breath, the old coordination remembered and not a change made again --- filed on the sixth place with no payer named, worth nothing at two inches of air (T061/T082). Emotional turn: a fourth asking makes a deeper hole in the silence without filling it, and the boy refuses to let four holes in a row stand up and call themselves a mouth. Last image: the voice goes off up the terrace while the row stands where it stood and the hand comes down with Sella's counted breath.

scenes.title: The Third Reading
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 239, Grain 30, Tenthday, the third and last Account-day and market of Grain. THE CHAPTER'S ONE MEANINGFUL CHANGE, advanced and not paid: Grain's third arithmetic is read over the basket and cannot be changed back. New day, new date, no recap: **239** exact, six months and fifty-nine days, nobody told (T071/T072); fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and thirty-nine days (T088); Grain 30 was one morning ahead at the close of the last scene and is not brought into a day that had not earned it. Sella carries him down at the half-pace, sets the basket in the moot-post's thin shade where no slate lies, stands half a pace off and gives no instruction or reason to the basket, and gives the wool and the river wind their words and never the basket (T058/T079). Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road to the reading block under the moot-post with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, hot clay over the smell of nothing at all; his large clean hands wipe the thumb twice before touching nothing, hold a narrow slate unopened to the forearm, pass a finger over the figure and let the eyes rest a breath longer than the writing requires, and read *one in twelve, as the notice says* low into the top of the crowd, the figure going twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that came late. He says *The levy is called. It is not called by me* and *your house*, never *I*, takes himself out of his own sentence as neatly as a surgeon withdraws a hand before the dressing goes on, and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness. The district's arithmetic changes for the third time in Grain and cannot be changed back; the printed figure stands unchallenged and a figure read aloud is still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047, T077). The bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, heard beside told (T078). Hessa Rale takes Berr's narrow slate up the clay road before noon, edge-on to her forearm and the writing turned to her sleeve, her hand to the slate before her eyes to the crowd, the second strap let out for the long road and the dried pale scurf unbrushed on the shortened skirt; to a woman who asks what she carries she says *I don't read it. I carry it. There's a difference, and the road doesn't care which* and answers the question put and not the one behind it; no figure comes off the slate and her order of reaching stays the eighth record-first hand on a place of its own, not joined to Berr's twice-wiped thumb, the soft-cuffed clerk's inward slate, Marra or any keeping (T080 advanced, not paid). Below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, slate to forearm and writing inward, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, the market sold over him as water goes over a stone that lies where a stone lies; nobody steps around him and nobody takes him off (T090). Across the square at the pot board the seventh green stays a colour at the silent woman's mouth --- clay in the nail crescents, a pale line across the back of one hand, sweet lead glaze in the crease beside her lip, a cup turned a quarter and set back exactly where it stood --- and at the market's edge the seventh shape stays a shape in cast-offs with a gap where a front tooth had been and a green sliver catching light and going dull; no eighth of either at Grain's last market, no second look joined, no name spoken over either, never Fenna or Ulda in the narration, no loaf, slate or sale and no romance paid (T050/T051 and T033/T034 held as sightings). The year's dressed grain lies under wool near the hearth with no figure over it, read over in the square by a figure that does not know what it cost, and the hand that went in on Seed 15 has no figure in the returning line (T077, T098 carried, not paid). The reading answers nothing for the man carried out on Day 188: no figure, collector, slate, cause, name or offstage death, and no name for what ailed him (T064). The hand is asked the fifth way at the market's edge and answers the **fifty-third** time --- held to the river's own low interval with no count in the house to borrow and down on the next low note --- filed on the sixth place with no payer named, not a hearing and not water-over-water promoted among the hearings (T061/T082). Sella carries him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what was read over him, goes around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face and leaves the thread frozen. Emotional turn: everything the district has withheld all month is gathered into one square and read over without a single one of the withholdings being named, so the market ends as it began, in arithmetic that does not balance. Last image: the basket goes home under the fold with the figure heard twice and the weight of neither carried into the house.

scenes.title: The Month Goes Out
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 239, Grain 30, Tenthday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the salt coat and hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. Grain goes out without a boundary drawn in the narration; neither of the district's two names for the months is corrected and Smoke is not brought into a day that has not earned it. The afternoon thins without ending; heat settles under the low angle, behind the pot, into the fold where one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust lies two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform (T061/T082). Garl is kept in objects and not in a story: salt-stiff coat, hollow seat with its twenty-year lean, the clean dark line and the finer grey called the thaw unswept, a proverb gone years ago to a pot with no crack, the tile debt circling without a name, his name unspoken two hundred and thirty-nine days; no collector came up or went down the clay road on Grain 28, 29 or 30 (T009/T013/T092). Sella gives the fire its instruction before the basket, tells it the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it* where another woman would say *I*, stands counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and leaves the widow's mark untouched --- no opening in **fifty-nine** days, because an afternoon, a shelf, a yard, a basket and a pot are not openings and Grain's third reading is not an opening (T058/T079, T100). The dressed grain stays covered and unfigured under wool near the hearth, counted in glances and handfuls and by a carrying arm that knows weight and not cost, entered on no slate (T077). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, sets the knife at the very edge with six where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there as a remembered stopping with nine stoppings and no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, draws the Seed 16 breath and does not spend it, and sweeps the collector's road without once turning along it; the warm stone lies cold and unreconciled in its loft pot, for not trying is not forgiving (T036/T076, T006). At the wheel-shed edge Jorra comes through with slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, speaks to the wheel before anyone and tells a pot *You'll do*, knows its note three turns ahead and withholds it, keeps the burned-slate word at four and the shut-room tellings at two, says neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, holds his bent finger in the damper ahead of Sella's sentence as a remembered repetition, keeps *he's not Vail* sealed and the promise of the boy's name neither given nor withdrawn, and gives the men who went into the back room before first grey no name (T035/T031/T062). In the small hours there is no breathing number anywhere in the house. Fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one: under the floor the carried fire gives four low pulls and withholds the fifth, its payer unnamed for two hundred and thirty-nine days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water; overhead the boards keep four nails on the near board, four on the next and a thumb-width knot where the fifth nail should have stood. A man who wanted the three to agree would have to put a payer under all of them, and none stands to any. He turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds it exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings of the full note beside and never among, five from four sources and the sixth out of a person, with no seventh in two hundred and thirty-nine days and none invented to fill the empty place, for an empty place kept empty is a finding and a finding filled to make a row come out even is a finding forged; three near-full answers advanced and unpaid; three shapings of the pot saying, the fourth burned-slate telling and the two shut-room tellings on their own places; told bell beside heard, four, four and a gap; told figure beside paid, and the figure read over the covered grain still not the figure paid, the true subtraction locked beyond this roof and answering nothing for the man carried out on Day 188; nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, and still ungiven; Seed 16 breath unspent and loan uncalled; three held changes on three places, the loft-sill scrape fourth, the carried man's pale line fifth and the held inch sixth; seventh green a colour and seventh shape a shape with no eighth, no name, no loaf, no slate and no sale; dressed grain covered and unfigured, returning-line place gone around with a look and no number; and on a seventh place of its own, with a finger between each pair and a finger between them and the sayings, tellings, hearings and count, the question standing with **four askings and no witness**, four askings still not one witness (T101). He puts the question to his hand the sixth way of the chapter. The hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the low note through the finger's-width door and stays. He takes it through the small intake, the hold and the letting go of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch his, keeps it through the little silence after her count has ended and brings it down on the river's next low note --- two rhythms, one held against the other across a wall that does not touch, remembered, not a change made again. He files the coordination on the sixth place with no payer named, and it is not spent or explained: not a longer reach, not a miss entered, not a hearing, not a seventh of the full note, not a tenth stopping, not a payment, not one of the held changes, not a key, not a power, not a rule. **Fifty-four** answers stand on that place now, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air (T061/T082). **Two hundred and thirty-nine** stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody in Sarn, Sill or Grath; six months and fifty-nine days told by nobody; the fire's fifth unpaid the same number of days; the widow's mark untouched with no opening in fifty-nine days; the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven. Grain's third and last reading is behind and unread under this roof and Smoke 1 stands three mornings ahead, not brought into a day that has not earned it. Emotional turn: the month closes the way it opened, with a kept file and an unspoken number, and the only movement is the count going forward. Last image: the hand comes down on the river's next low note, the file lies open on the towel complete and worth nothing, and the count goes forward exact and unspent into a day that has not yet earned its heading --- Day 240, Smoke 1, Firstday, which belongs to the next chapter.
